problems.title: Amdahl
problems.statement: A fraction p of an application is accelerated by s.

problems.title: Budget first
problems.statement: An application: 40 ms copying data, 50 ms in kernels, 10 ms host code. You make the kernels 2× faster.
problems.solution: 75 ms: 1.33×. Overlapping the copies (Chapter 7.3) would have been worth more.

problems.title: Decomposition choice
hints: Few outputs and many inputs versus balanced.
problems.solution: 256 bins can't occupy a GPU, so histograms go input-centric with privatisation; blur and potential maps gather.

problems.title: Dynamic parallelism threshold
problems.statement: A device-side launch costs 5 µs; a thread processes a small region inline at 0.01 µs per element.

parts.prompt: Region size above which a child launch is worth it (break-even, ignoring the child's parallel speedup)?

hints: Compare inline time with launch cost.
problems.solution: Below about 500 elements inline is cheaper than even launching; real thresholds are higher once the child's own overhead is included.

problems.title: Unified memory faults
problems.statement: A kernel touches 1 GB of managed memory that starts on the host; each 64 KB fault migration costs 20 µs.

parts.prompt: Explicit prefetch at 25 GB/s, in ms?

problems.solution: 16,384 faults ≈ 328 ms, against 43 ms for a prefetch: prefetch hints matter.

problems.title: Library or custom
problems.statement: When should you write your own kernel instead of calling a library?

options: To fuse operations the library runs separately
For an unusual data type or shape it handles badly
When a measurement shows the library is the bottleneck and a better design exists

problems.solution: Fusion, special types and measured gaps; not by default.

problems.title: Strong scaling
problems.statement: A problem of fixed size takes 100 ms on 1 GPU; 5 ms of it is serial setup.

parts.prompt: Best time on 8 GPUs with perfect scaling of the rest, in ms?

problems.title: Which bound first
problems.statement: A new kernel does 10 GFLOP and moves 2 GB on a GPU with 20 TFLOP/s and 1 TB/s.
hints: Compare the two bounds before writing code.
problems.solution: Memory-bound by 4×: reduce bytes (fusion, layout, precision) first.

problems.title: Cooperative groups

options: all blocks are guaranteed resident (cooperative launch)

problems.solution: A grid-wide barrier deadlocks unless every block runs at once.

problems.title: Designing from scratch
problems.statement: Compute, for 10⁶ queries, the 10 nearest of 10⁶ reference points in 3-D.

options: Spatial binning of reference points (like cutoff binning)
Per-query top-10 in registers or a small sorting network
A dense 10⁶ × 10⁶ distance matrix in memory
Gather: a thread (or warp) per query

problems.solution: Bin, gather per query, keep a running top-k in registers. A 10¹² dense matrix (4 TB) is out.
